record.title: Compose ownership names can collide for distinct experiment identifiers
record.description: ComposeAdapter normalizes project and experiment identifiers by replacing every non-lowercase-alphanumeric/hyphen run with a hyphen. Distinct experiment IDs such as exp/a and exp-a can therefore receive the same project, network, and volume names, making concurrent lifecycle operations address the same resources.
record.claimed_root_cause: The ownership namespace is derived from lossy normalization without validating or hashing the experiment identifier for collision resistance.

trace.description: The adapter accepts an experiment_id used to derive external resource names.
The experiment ID is passed through lossy regex substitution and stripped.
The normalized string becomes the Compose project, network, and volume ownership namespace.

evidence.description: _SAFE replaces non-alphanumeric/hyphen runs with a single hyphen.
The normalized project and experiment values directly form all three resource names.
Tests verify a normal unique name but do not cover colliding identifiers or concurrent experiments.

blockers: No sandboxed Compose runtime was available, so resource collision and cross-cleanup behavior were not exercised.
The repository does not show whether experiment_id is attacker-controlled or globally unique before adapter construction.

validation_plan.local: In an isolated fake-runner test, construct adapters for exp/a and exp-a and assert their ownership names; in a sandboxed Compose fixture, verify concurrent start/stop cannot affect the other experiment.
validation_plan.deployment: Confirm experiment ID generation and whether multiple principals can start experiments concurrently against a shared Docker daemon.

record.title: CLI import reads complete files before the importer byte limit
record.description: The public import command reads both baseline and candidate files with Path.read_text before calling import_otlp_json. The importer enforces max_bytes only after the complete text object already exists, so an oversized local input can consume memory before it is rejected.
record.claimed_root_cause: The size limit is enforced at the parser boundary after unbounded file reads instead of before or during bounded streaming reads.

trace.description: CLI accepts caller-selected baseline and candidate paths and reads each file as text.
The complete candidate text is passed to import_otlp_json after the read has completed.
The max_bytes check occurs only after the full text argument and its UTF-8 encoding are already allocated.

evidence.description: Path.read_text has no pre-read size check or bounded read.
The importer rejects oversized input only after receiving the full string.
Importer tests cover logical max_spans and malformed data but do not exercise a bounded CLI file read under resource limits.

blockers: The required resource-limited sandbox was unavailable, so memory behavior was not measured with an oversized file.
The current CLI is a local command and the repository does not define whether untrusted users can submit import files to a shared process.

validation_plan.local: In the required resource-limited sandbox, provide a sparse or generated oversized input file to the CLI and observe bounded rejection versus process memory growth; do not exceed the minimum needed to establish the result.
validation_plan.deployment: Confirm whether import runs on a shared service or only for a trusted local operator; if shared, treat file size as attacker-controlled input.

phase5_nonmaterial_correction.reason: The rejected verdict, local CLI boundary, sequential full reads and cost scope are source-grounded. Correct sanitizer evidence precision: the 512-character truncation applies to strings and converted objects, while booleans and numeric values pass through unchanged at sanitizer.py:28-35. All cited files and importer call sites were re-read; no target execution occurred.
phase5_nonmaterial_correction.classification: Nonmaterial factual precision only; verdict, root cause, trace, input, observed result, impact and severity unchanged. Parent re-read cited current source.

record.title: Declared scenario and execution limits are not enforced by all consumers
record.description: The schema validates finite limits and Scenario carries samples, concurrency, and timeout values, but ScenarioRunner iterates scenario.warmup and scenario.samples directly and does not apply limits.max_samples or limits.max_concurrency. A configuration or integration that treats those limits as enforcement could receive substantially more work than intended.
record.claimed_root_cause: Limits are represented in separate configuration objects without a single enforcement point connecting RepositoryConfig.limits to ScenarioRunner execution.

trace.description: The configuration model exposes finite max_samples and max_concurrency controls.
Scenario stores samples and concurrency independently from the limits object.
Execution loops use scenario.warmup and scenario.samples directly, with no repository-limit check.

evidence.description: max_samples is a validated finite setting but is not attached to ScenarioRunner.
max_concurrency is validated but the runner has no concurrency-limit parameter or enforcement.
The measured loop trusts scenario.samples directly.

blockers: The current integration does not expose a complete end-to-end path that passes RepositoryConfig.limits into ScenarioRunner.
The target sandbox was unavailable, so no resource-limited local run was performed.

validation_plan.local: Construct a configuration with scenario.samples above limits.max_samples and run the actual orchestration path in a no-network resource-limited sandbox; verify whether it rejects before requests or performs the excess iterations.
validation_plan.deployment: Confirm whether untrusted configuration authors can select scenario counts or whether configurations are trusted operator input.

phase5_nonmaterial_correction.reason: The rejection is source-grounded, but its reason incorrectly describes the current first trace element as a dataclass; the current trace starts at ScenarioRunner.run. Replace that stale characterization with the actual caller-supplied Scenario and callback authority.
phase5_nonmaterial_correction.classification: Nonmaterial factual precision only; verdict, root cause, trace, input, observed result, impact and severity unchanged. Parent re-read cited current source.

record.title: Artifact resolution may cross project or experiment boundaries through symlinks
record.description: OwnedStorage binds a handle to a project identifier, but resolves the requested artifact through filesystem links and checks containment only against the shared storage home. A link inside one project can therefore resolve into another project or experiment that remains below that home.
record.claimed_root_cause: The final containment invariant is shared-home containment rather than containment beneath the selected experiment root, and link traversal is not rejected.

trace.description: A caller supplies project, experiment, and a relative artifact path.
The requested relative path is appended to the experiment root and passed to _owned.
Path.resolve follows links and only checks that the resolved path remains under self.home.

evidence.description: Project binding validates the supplied project name but does not bind the resolved path to that project root.
The shared-home containment check accepts a resolved link target in another project under the same home.
The existing symlink test covers escape outside the home, not a link from one project into another project within the home.

blockers: The required OS-enforced sandbox was unavailable, so a disposable two-project symlink fixture was not executed.
The deployment contract does not establish whether untrusted users or processes can create links in the evidence home.

validation_plan.local: In an isolated, no-network, read-only-target sandbox, create two project trees under a disposable storage home, place a link in project A targeting project B, and verify whether resolve('project-a', ...) returns a B path; also test link creation permissions.
validation_plan.deployment: Confirm the evidence home is not writable by a lower-trust principal and that artifact readers require experiment-root containment rather than shared-home containment.
